title: What Generative Artificial Intelligence Means for Terminological Definitions
venue: 3rd International Conference on Multilingual digital terminology today. Design, representation formats and management systems
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative artificial intelligence, especially ChatGPT and other large language model-based tools, may change terminological definition writing and the broader field of terminography. The central problem addressed is that traditional terminological definitions are labor-intensive to produce, especially when they must reflect contextual and functional constraints rather than only universal characteristics. The author argues that GenAI can reduce the time and effort required to create definitions, while also raising questions about whether human-made terminological resources will remain necessary in the same form.

The paper does not report an empirical intervention study. Instead, it offers a conceptual discussion of AI-assisted terminography, with emphasis on post-editing workflows in which a machine generates a definition and the terminologist revises it. It also describes other support uses, such as asking ChatGPT to explain terminology in context, analyze existing definitions, extract semantic traits from corpora or concordances, and assess or refine draft definitions. The context is professional terminology work rather than classroom instruction, and the intended users are terminologists and other terminology professionals.

The main conclusion is that AI is likely to become integrated into terminology workflows and may improve efficiency and possibly quality, especially by making flexible, context-sensitive definitions easier to produce. At the same time, the paper stresses that GenAI output can be unreliable, biased, or hallucinatory, so human verification remains important. The author concludes that AI-assisted terminography will probably become a standard part of terminology practice, with the line between human-created and AI-generated content becoming increasingly blurred.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical review and position paper about GenAI in terminological definition writing, not an empirical study. It does not report a research design, comparison groups, or measured outcomes relevant to the requested evidence framework.
impact_tier_rationale: No causal impact estimates or outcome data are reported, so there is no measurable evidence of effect on teaching, planning, or feedback quality. The paper only argues that GenAI could improve efficiency and quality in future terminology work.
